title: ATP-driven membrane binding and polymerization of bacterial actin MreB promotes local membrane fluidization
authors: Adriaans IE; Álvarez-Mena A; Dinet C; Morvan E; Lim KS; Dufourc EJ; Wong R; Chastanet A; Michelot A; Carballido-López R; Habenstein B
one_liner_zh: 该文研究细菌肌动蛋白MreB与脂膜的ATP驱动结合及聚合，涉及膜结合机制但对象非无序蛋白/IDR，且无AI或物理模拟方法，仅与膜互作机制部分相关。
abstract:
The bacterial actin homologue MreB plays a key role in rod cell shape determination. We recently showed that MreB from the Gram-positive bacterium Geobacillus stearothermophilus (MreB Gs ) polymerizes into straight pairs of protofilaments in the presence of both ATP and a lipid surface. Membrane interaction is thought to be mediated by electrostatic interactions with anionic lipids, with final anchoring relying on two spatially close hydrophobic motifs that protrude from the MreB Gs monomers, forming a putative membrane-insertion domain. Here, we determined the binding properties of ATP and ADP to MreB Gs using fluorescence anisotropy, and monitored ATP-mediated binding and polymer formation on lipid bilayers using liposome binding assays and AFM, respectively. Finally, we used solid-state NMR to visualize the interaction between the membrane and MreB Gs at the atomic level. Our findings reveal that MreB Gs has similar affinity for both ATP and ADP, unlike eukaryotic actin. We also show that monomeric MreB Gs establishes peripheral contacts with the membrane likely through electrostatic interactions, while ATP-induced MreB Gs filaments insert into the lipid bilayer without interfering with the membrane lamellar phase and have a significant local fluidifying effect.

Statement of significance

Bacteria rely on the actin-like protein MreB to determine and maintain their cell shape, like actin does in eukaryotic cells. To perform its tightly regulated morphogenetic function, MreB forms membrane-associated nanofilaments in vivo , which control the cell wall biosynthetic machinery. We recently demonstrated that, in vitro , MreB from the Gram-positive bacterium Geobacillus stearothermophilus requires both ATP and lipids to polymerize into pairs of filaments. Here, we show that in the presence of ATP, Geobacillus MreB forms membrane-bound filaments that directly impact local membrane fluidity, which could translate into a regulatory effect on cell wall synthetic enzymes. We further reveal that MreB binds both ATP and ADP with similar affinity, unlike eukaryotic actin, which preferentially binds ATP over ADP, and speculate that this could be a mechanism modulating the pool of polymerization-competent MreB in bacteria.
abstract_zh:
细菌肌动蛋白同源物MreB在杆状细胞形态决定中发挥关键作用。我们近期研究表明，来自革兰氏阳性菌嗜热脂肪土芽孢杆菌（Geobacillus stearothermophilus）的MreB（MreB Gs）在ATP和脂质表面同时存在时，聚合形成直的原丝纤维对。膜相互作用被认为由阴离子脂质的静电相互作用介导，最终锚定依赖于两个空间上接近的疏水基序，这些基序从MreB Gs单体突出，形成假定的膜插入结构域。在此，我们利用荧光各向异性测定了ATP和ADP与MreB Gs的结合特性，并分别通过脂质体结合实验和原子力显微镜（AFM）监测了ATP介导的脂质双层上的结合和聚合物形成。最后，我们使用固态核磁共振（solid-state NMR）在原子水平上可视化膜与MreB Gs之间的相互作用。我们的发现揭示，MreB Gs对ATP和ADP具有相似的亲和力，这与真核肌动蛋白不同。我们还表明，单体MreB Gs可能通过静电相互作用与膜建立外周接触，而ATP诱导的MreB Gs丝插入脂质双层而不干扰膜层状相，并具有显著的局部流化效应。

意义声明

细菌依赖肌动蛋白样蛋白MreB来确定和维持其细胞形态，正如肌动蛋白在真核细胞中所起的作用。为执行其严格调控的形态发生功能，MreB在体内形成膜相关纳米丝，这些丝控制细胞壁生物合成机制。我们近期证明，在体外，来自革兰氏阳性菌嗜热脂肪土芽孢杆菌的MreB需要ATP和脂质才能聚合形成丝对。在此，我们表明在ATP存在下，嗜热脂肪土芽孢杆菌MreB形成膜结合丝，直接影响局部膜流动性，这可能转化为对细胞壁合成酶的调控效应。我们进一步揭示，MreB以相似亲和力结合ATP和ADP，这与优先结合ATP而非ADP的真核肌动蛋白不同，并推测这可能是调节细菌中聚合能力MreB库的一种机制。
